excluded.reason: Dry or raw staples (rice, pasta, beans, chickpeas, lentils). Every POF measure for them is of the COOKED food (e.g. 'Macarrão cozido - colher de sopa cheia', 'Arroz - prato fundo raso'), but TACO reports the raw product: applying cooked grams to raw per-100 g values would overstate nutrients by roughly 2-3x. The cooked rice and bean entries already map to the cooked TACO foods. TACO has no cooked pasta and no cooked chickpeas, so those foods answer 'no household measures' instead of a wrong number.
Wheat flour has no POF measures; the 'FUBA DE MILHO' rows are of cooked angu and the 'AMIDO DE MILHO' row is of a cooked mingau.
Source is another product: Corn Flakes for sugar-coated flakes, prepared cream for powdered corn cream, a prepared lasagna dish for fresh lasagna pasta, cooked angu for pre-cooked polenta.
Raw foods whose POF rows are all described as cooked (e.g. 'Chuchu cozido - unidade média', 'Ovo de galinha cozido'); the POF preparation code says 'cru' but the source description does not.
Chicken pieces: POF weights are of pieces with bone (asa, coxa, peito), TACO values are per 100 g of edible portion.
POF rows are of a different flavor or variety (wafer and filled biscuit of chocolate; banana prata unit weights).
